"Blood & Vomit" is a 2004 studio album by black metal artist Nattefrost (Norwegian for Night Frost). This is his first solo work, as he is mainly known for being frontman for Carpathian Forest, formed in 1992.

Now, listening to this, we start off with a lot heavier black metal then at least I am used to, being more fond of the ambient and synth part of black metal, with maybe some exceptions. And frankly, I just did not like this record. Maybe I just didn't have the spark for it, but it just bored me. "Satanic Victory" and "Sanctum 666" is the only songs that I really "noticed". The rest of the record was just noise, with some pissing or vomiting in between. Black metal is supposed to be "Disliked" especially towards the average 40 year old white Christian woman. Its supposed to be repulsive and devilish, but this just felt insanely performative to me. Decent 1.

extras.notes:
"Chore Of Enchantment" is a americana, alt country album released in 1999 by Giant Sand. Arizona based band was first started by singer/songwriter and solo artist Howe Gelb, and this certainly is not their first album. Dating back to 1980, when the band was first started, they had already released 8 full length studio albums and cycled through many, many different members. This specific album has Howe Gelb on vocals, guitar, and piano, Joey Burns (Calexico)  on bass and John Convertino (Calexico) on drums. 

Now, listening to this, we start with a relatively strong and interesting start, a short intro for the record, dramatic and weird use of various noises that goes into the next song "(Well) Dusted". well dusted is one of my more liked tracks on this record, good guitar and bass work, with Howe's vocals in a sort of mumbling style I kind of like. Quite similar with the track "X-Tra Wide", which brings a more mellow, relaxed tone. Some other standout tracks like "Wolfy" and even "Astonished (In Memphis)" appeal to me in some way, but other times I felt most of these tracks landing flat for me. The vocals sometimes felt to strong, and almost even uncomfortable. Overall, this just did not appeal to me, even if they were maybe 2 or so tracks that were alright, its not something I am going to come back to. Decent 1.

"The Black Light" is a full length studio album released in 1998 by American indie rock band Calexico. Calexico first formed in Arizona with frontmen Joey Burns and John Convertino when they met in college, studying music. They played in other bands before, noticeably Giant Sand with Howe Gelb and Friends of Dean Martinez with Bill Elm.

Now, The Black Light is an album that contains songs that hit harder for me, that i heard when i was a still a kid, and might be sort of biased to. the songs that really standout on this record for me are "Stray" and "Bloodflow", which bring this dark and almost sinister tone to the album, with this gothic, americana, almost western vibe to it. The record feels very heavily inspired by traditional "mariachi" originating from 18th and 19th century Mexico. We have some more mysterious, sort of funkier instrumentals in between, which overall gives the album some more surface and variety. I think its brings a good variety of sounds, meaningful instrumentals, and solid songwriting. Even though I like the style of the album, and how its structured, the amount of songs I might come back to listen to, is sort of limited. Stray, Bloodflow, Chach and Old Man Waltz is what sticks with me the most. Solid album, good listening experience, but cannot guarantee I would come back to praise it after a year or so. Decent 3.

albumTitle: In The Court Of The Crimson King (Expanded & Remastered Original Album Mix)

extras.notes:
"Figure 8" is a full length studio album released in 2000 by beloved singer/songwriter Elliott Smith. Smith began performing in bands early on in highschool, and eventually formed punk-ish rock band Heatmiser with Neil Gust.

Now, this album was weird for me, because I had known the history of Elliot Smith, how much people loved his work and especially this album. I like to think I gave this album its fair tries, and honestly, it just did not land for me. I think there are some pretty solid tracks off this record, "Happines/The Gondola Man" brings some great vocal performance and songwriting, same with "Son Of Sam" and "Everything Means Nothing To Me". But there were times were I felt a lot of songs to fall flat for me, where the songs just felt nihilistic in some way. I can understand why people really like this record, and I wont deny that he had talent for music. Decent 2.
